text:
Lina: FYI PulseMed reached out — they got a $12,400 'burst usage' charge on this month's dedicated invoice despite their 6000-token commit. They say this didn't happen last month.
Owen: Can you drop the invoice link?
Lina: https://billing.redwood.example/invoices/inv_987654 — key lines below:
```
line_items:
  - sku: dedicated_commit_6k  amount: $0  usage: 6,050 tokens
  - sku: burst_overage      amount: $12,400 usage: 120k tokens
```
Pulse says commit should have covered the first 60k tokens.
Devon: I pulled account config — their account has a live experiment flag `pricing_v2_burst_override` set on 1769985000. That variant flips matching order so burst rules can get applied before commit buckets.
Sandeep: That was one of the 5-account targeted experiments we rolled to test burst discounts + alternative attribution. PulseMed was intentionally included. The intent was to give them burst discounts, not to bypass commit coverage. Looks like the attribution order bug flipped.
Devon: If attribution is wrong we need to both fix the logic and credit PulseMed. Rough calc: they were charged $12,400; with correct matching we estimate $2,700 would have been charged (net $9,700 credit). I'll run precise reconciliation.
billing-bot: Invoice generated invoice_987654 total:$12,400  created:1769988000  customer:pulsemed
QA-ops: I can open a quick patch to the billing matcher to prioritize dedicated commit buckets. I can push PR + run unit tests, then roll it behind the experiment gate.
Owen: Action items: (1) manual credit for PulseMed today, (2) scan all accounts with `pricing_v2_burst_override` for misbilling, (3) revert/patch experiment logic.
Devon: Agreed. I'll create credit note for $9,700 and append a line on the invoice explaining the correction. I'll also run account-scan and drop results into #finance-recon by EOD. :white_check_mark:
Lina: Please confirm SLA calculations — does this affect SLA credits or was it only pricing attribution? I'll hold external comms until we know.
Devon: Confirmed SLA metrics unchanged — capacity and latency logs show no breach; this is purely billing attribution.
Sandeep: Sales: we'll offer PulseMed a goodwill gesture (one month free Dedicated or equivalent) if they're unhappy. Keep me updated on the customer reply.
Lina: Thanks everyone. I'll message PulseMed once the credit posts and include a short explanation and next steps. Closing thread after credit is posted.
